sentences.chinese: 令地方一里爲井，井十爲通，通十爲成，成方十里。
sentences.literal: [They] ordered that land be measured: one li square makes one well-field unit (jing); ten jing make a tong; ten tong make a cheng; one cheng spans ten li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Under the statute, one square li formed a jing, ten jing made a tong, ten tong a cheng, and a cheng stood ten li to the side.

sentences.chinese: 成十爲終，終十爲同，同方百里。
sentences.literal: Ten cheng make a zhong; ten zhong make a tong; one tong extends one hundred li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: A stack of ten cheng became a zhong; ten zhong a tong, and each tong measured a hundred li on a side.

sentences.chinese: 同十爲封，封十爲畿，畿方千里。
sentences.literal: Ten tong make a feng; ten feng make a ji; a ji spans one thousand li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Ten tong made a feng; ten feng a royal ringland (ji), a thousand li on every side—the core demesne of the crown.

sentences.chinese: 故井四爲邑，邑四爲丘，丘十六井，有戎馬一匹，牛三頭。
sentences.literal: Therefore four jing make a settlement (yi); four yi make a mound-district (qiu); a qiu holds sixteen jing, with one war-horse and three oxen.
sentences.idiomatic: So four jing grouped into a yi, four yi into a qiu holding sixteen jing, supporting one mount for war and three draft oxen.

sentences.chinese: 四丘爲甸，甸六十四井也，有戎馬四匹，兵車一乘，牛十二頭，甲士三人，卒七十二人。
sentences.literal: Four qiu make a dian; a dian is sixty-four jing, with four war-horses, one war-chariot, twelve oxen, three armored warriors, and seventy-two foot soldiers.
sentences.idiomatic: Four qiu formed a dian of sixty-four jing, fit for four chargers, a single battle chariot, twelve oxen, three armored men, and seventy-two rank-and-file troops.

sentences.chinese: 是謂乘車之制。
sentences.literal: This is called the rule for holding a chariot.
sentences.idiomatic: This defined the military levy for one chariot.

sentences.chinese: 一同百里，提封萬井，除山川、坑岸、城池、邑居、園囿、街路三千六百井，定出賦六千四百井，戎馬四百匹，兵車百乘，此卿大夫菜地之大者也，是謂百乘之家。
sentences.literal: One tong measures one hundred li square; its tifeng is ten thousand jing; after removing mountains, rivers, pits, banks, walls and moats of cities, towns and residences, parks and enclosures, and thoroughfares—three thousand six hundred jing—the taxable assessment fixes six thousand four hundred jing, four hundred war-horses, and one hundred chariots; this is the greatest among ministers' and grandees' provision fiefs, called a house of one hundred chariots.
sentences.idiomatic: For a single tong, a hundred li on a side and ten thousand jing under seal, once mountains, waters, wasteland, fortifications, settlements, hunting parks, and roads had been set aside—three thousand six hundred jing—the remaining sixty-four hundred jing furnished four hundred mounts and a full hundred chariots; that was the largest estate granted to ministers and great officers, the so-called household of a hundred chariots.

sentences.chinese: 一封三百六十六里，提封十萬井，定出賦六萬四千井，戎馬四千匹，兵車千乘，此謂諸侯之大者也，謂之千乘之國。
sentences.literal: One feng measures three hundred sixty-six li square; its tifeng is one hundred thousand jing; the taxable assessment fixes sixty-four thousand jing, four thousand war-horses, and one thousand chariots; this is called a great feudal lord, termed a state of a thousand chariots.
sentences.idiomatic: A feng of three hundred sixty-six li to the side embraced a hundred thousand jing, with sixty-four thousand taxable jing sustaining four thousand horses and a thousand chariots—the scale of the greatest feudal lords, a true thousand-chariot polity.

sentences.chinese: 天子畿內方千里，提封百萬井，定出賦六十四萬井，戎馬四萬匹，兵車萬乘，戎卒七十二萬人，故天子稱萬乘之主焉。
sentences.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's ji, a thousand li square, the tifeng is a million jing; the taxable assessment fixes six hundred forty thousand jing, forty thousand war-horses, ten thousand chariots, and seven hundred twenty thousand troops; therefore the Son of Heaven is called lord of ten thousand chariots.
sentences.idiomatic: Across the royal thousand-li square, a million jing yielded taxable ground for sixty-four myriad jing, mounting forty thousand horses, ten thousand chariots, and seven hundred twenty thousand soldiers—whence the sovereign earned the title of ruler of ten thousand chariots.

sentences.chinese: 秦始皇既得志於天下，訪周之敗，以爲處士橫議，諸侯尋戈，四夷交侵，以弱見奪，於是削去五等焉。
sentences.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin had realized his ambition in All-under-Heaven, he reviewed Zhou's defeat and took it that recluses bandied reckless opinions, feudal lords raised halberds one upon another, the four outer peoples invaded in turn, and Zhou, through weakness, was stripped away; thereupon he abolished the five noble ranks.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Qin Shihuang had mastered the realm, he read Zhou's fall as the fruit of unbridled private debate among scholars, incessant war among lords, and relentless barbarian pressure that preyed on weakness—and scrapped the entire five-rank aristocracy.

sentences.chinese: 漢興，創艾亡秦孤立而敗，於是割裂封疆，立爵二等，功臣侯者百有餘邑。
sentences.literal: When Han rose, [rulers] learned from the wound of fallen Qin's isolation and collapse; therefore they carved territory into enfeoffments, set up two grades of nobility, and merit marquises held more than a hundred towns.
sentences.idiomatic: Han, still smarting from Qin's rigid centralization and swift ruin, reapportioned the map into fiefs, limited noble rank to two tiers, and let more than a hundred merit marquises each hold a patch of soil.

sentences.chinese: 于時民罹秦項，戶口彫弊，大侯不過萬家，小者五六百戶，而尊王子弟，大啟九國。
sentences.literal: At that time the people had suffered under Qin and Xiang; households and population were depleted; great marquises did not exceed ten thousand households, small ones five or six hundred households; yet [the court] honored imperial sons and younger brothers and vastly opened up nine kingdoms.
sentences.idiomatic: Households were still shattered by Qin exactions and Chu civil war, so even great marquisates counted fewer than ten thousand families and small ones only five or six hundred—yet the throne lavished titles on imperial kinsmen and planted nine sprawling royal domains.

sentences.chinese: 古者有分土而無分民，若乃大者跨州連郡，小則十有餘城，以戶口爲差降，略封疆之遠近，所謂分民自漢始也。
sentences.literal: In antiquity there was division of land but no division of people; but in this case the large [fiefs] spanned provinces and linked commanderies, the small had ten-odd cities, and [status] was graded by registered households, neglecting how far the borders lay; what is called dividing the people begins with Han.
sentences.idiomatic: Ancient kings had parceled soil, not registered subjects; now the largest apanages covered whole provinces, the modest still held a dozen walled towns, and rank tracked headcounts while the distances of frontiers hardly mattered—the peculiar Han practice of parting the people among lords had begun.

sentences.chinese: 起雁門以東，盡遼陽，爲燕代。
sentences.literal: From Yanmen eastward to the farthest reach of Liaoyang—this formed Yan and Dai.
sentences.idiomatic: The block running east from the Yanmen line through Liaoyang was reckoned as Yan and Dai together.

sentences.chinese: 常山以南，太行左轉，渡河濟，漸于海，爲齊趙。
sentences.literal: South of Mount Chang, the Taihang turning left, crossing the He and Ji [rivers], reaching to the sea—this formed Qi and Zhao.
sentences.idiomatic: South of Changshan, with the Taihang swinging east, the Yellow River and Ji ford behind them, and the coast ahead, stretched Qi and Zhao as one bloc.

sentences.chinese: 穀泗以注，奄有龜蒙，爲梁楚。
sentences.literal: Where the Gu and Si flow in, covering Gui and Meng—this formed Liang and Chu.
sentences.idiomatic: Between the Gu and Si confluence and the Gui-Meng massif lay the territories reckoned as Liang and Chu.

sentences.chinese: 東帶江湖，薄會稽，爲荊吳。
sentences.literal: Belted to the east by the Yangtze and lakes, pressing against Kuaiji—this formed Jing and Wu.
sentences.idiomatic: A strip belted by the great river and southern lakes, nosing to Kuaiji, counted as Jing and Wu.

sentences.chinese: 北界淮瀕，略廬衡，爲淮南。
sentences.literal: Bordered on the north by the Huai shore, taking in Lu and Heng—this formed Huainan.
sentences.idiomatic: North along the Huai's bank, drawing in the Lu and Heng ranges, stood the block called Huainan.

sentences.chinese: 波漢之陽，亙九疑，爲長沙。
sentences.literal: Beyond the northern bank of the Han, spanning the Jiuyi—this formed Changsha.
sentences.idiomatic: North of the Han sweep and through the Jiuyi peaks ran the Changsha alignment.

sentences.chinese: 諸侯比境，周匝三垂，外接胡越。
sentences.literal: The feudal lords shared adjoining borders; they wrapped the three outer margins; outward they connected to Hu and Yue.
sentences.idiomatic: The vassals stood shoulder to shoulder along the inner rim, girdling three frontiers while opening outward onto the Hu steppe and southern Yue.

sentences.chinese: 天子自有三河、東郡、潁川、南陽，自江陵以西至巴蜀，北至雲中，西至隴西，與京師內史，凡十五郡。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven himself held the Three He, Dong commandery, Yingchuan, Nanyang; from Jiangling west to Ba and Shu; north to Yunzhong; west to Longxi; together with the capital Neishi—in all fifteen commanderies.
sentences.idiomatic: Fifteen commanderies—the Three He core plus Dong, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, the western arc from Jiangling through Ba and Shu, the northern bastions Yunzhong, the Longxi line, and the metropolitan Neishi—remained directly in the emperor's hand.

sentences.chinese: 文帝采賈生之議分齊趙，景帝用朝錯之計削吳楚。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wen adopted Jia Yi's proposal to divide Qi and Zhao; Emperor Jing employed Chao Cuo's plan to pare away Wu and Chu.
sentences.idiomatic: Han Wendi split Qi and Zhao on Jia Yi's advice; Jingdi pared the great eastern kingdoms with Chao Cuo's stratagem.

sentences.chinese: 武帝施主父之冊，下推恩之令，使諸侯王得分戶邑以封子弟，不行黜陟，而藩國自析。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wu applied Zhufu Yi's memorial and issued the order to push favor outward, causing kings of the feudal states to divide household-towns to enfeoff sons and younger brothers; without carrying out demotions or promotions, the buffer kingdoms split of themselves.
sentences.idiomatic: Wudi promulgated Zhufu Yi's memorial as the "push-the-grace" edict, letting every king slice his domain to enfeoff heirs—no formal downgrading needed—and watched the great apanages quietly fracture.

sentences.chinese: 自此以來，齊分爲七，趙分爲六，梁分爲五，淮南分爲三。
sentences.literal: From this time on, Qi split into seven, Zhao into six, Liang into five, Huainan into three.
sentences.idiomatic: Thereafter Qi splintered seven ways, Zhao six, Liang five, Huainan three.

sentences.chinese: 皇子始立者大國不過十餘城，長沙、燕、代雖有舊名，皆亡南北邊矣。
sentences.literal: When imperial sons were first established, great states had no more than ten-odd cities; Changsha, Yan, and Dai, though bearing old names, had all lost their northern and southern frontiers.
sentences.idiomatic: A freshly minted imperial son might rule barely a dozen counties; mighty old names like Changsha, Yan, and Dai had become hollow titles stripped of their former north and south marches.

sentences.chinese: 自文景與民休息，至平帝元始二年，民戶千二百二十三萬三千六十二，口五千九百五十九萬四千九百七十八，其地東西九千三百二里，南北萬三千三百六十八里。
sentences.literal: From Wen and Jing, who rested the people, to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year: twelve million two hundred thirty-three thousand sixty-two households; fifty-nine million five hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred seventy-eight persons; the territory nine thousand three hundred two li east-west, thirteen thousand three hundred sixty-eight li north-south.
sentences.idiomatic: The restorative reigns of Wen and Jing carried down to Pingdi's Yuanshi 2 (1 CE), when the registers recorded 12,233,062 households and 59,594,978 people across 9,302 li east–west and 13,368 li north–south.

sentences.chinese: 大率十里一亭，亭有長。
sentences.literal: In general, one ting every ten li; a ting has a chief.
sentences.idiomatic: Roughly every ten li stood a courier lodge (ting) headed by a chief.

sentences.chinese: 十亭一鄉，鄉有三老，有秩嗇夫、游徼各一人。
sentences.literal: Ten ting make one xiang; a xiang has three elders, one ranked sefu, and one patrol officer (youjiao), one each.
sentences.idiomatic: Ten ting formed a township with three elders plus a single salaried sefu and a roving constable.

sentences.chinese: 縣大率方百里，民稠則減，稀則曠，鄉亭亦如之。
sentences.literal: Counties were generally one hundred li square; if people were dense it was reduced, if sparse it was expanded; xiang and ting likewise.
sentences.idiomatic: A county normally covered a hundred-li square, trimmed where crowded, widened where thin, township and lodge scales following suit.

sentences.chinese: 皆秦制也。
sentences.literal: All were Qin institutions.
sentences.idiomatic: Every one of these rules descended from Qin.

sentences.chinese: 光武中興，不踰前制，東海王彊以去就有禮，故優以大封，兼食魯郡二十九縣，其餘稱爲寵錫者，兼一郡而已。
sentences.literal: At Guangwu's restoration [the system] did not exceed prior norms; the Prince of Donghai, Qiang, for his proper bearing in choosing to stay or go, was therefore favored with a great enfeoffment, also drawing sustenance from twenty-nine counties of Lu commandery; the rest who were said to receive doted grants merely added one commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: When Guangwu revived Han he held to the old ceilings—except Liu Qiang, Prince of Donghai, whose scrupulous conduct in yielding the crown earned him a double stipend through twenty-nine Lu counties while other favorites merely tacked on a single commandery.

sentences.chinese: 至桓帝永壽三年，戶千六十七萬七千九百六十，口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六，[3]斯亦戶口之滋殖者也。
sentences.literal: Reaching Emperor Huan's Yongshou third year: ten million six hundred seventy-seven thousand nine hundred sixty households; fifty-six million four hundred eighty-six thousand eight hundred fifty-six persons; this too was the increase and multiplication of registered population.
sentences.idiomatic: By Huan's Yongshou 3 (157 CE) the rolls listed 10,677,960 households and 56,486,856 souls—clear evidence that the people were breeding back.

sentences.chinese: 獻帝建安元年拜曹操爲鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。
sentences.literal: In Emperor Xian's Jian'an first year [the court] appointed Cao Cao General Who Stabilizes the East and enfeoffed him Marquis of the Feiting precinct.
sentences.idiomatic: In Xian's first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao received appointment as General Who Stabilizes the East and an enfeoffment as Marquis of the Feiting precinct.

sentences.chinese: 魏文帝黃初三年，初制封王之庶子爲鄉公，嗣王之庶子爲亭侯，[4]公侯之庶子爲亭伯。
sentences.literal: In Wei Wendi's Huangchu third year, an edict first ruled that the king's sons by secondary wives became xiang dukes, the heir-king's sons by secondary wives became ting marquises, and the sons by secondary wives of dukes and marquises became ting earls.
sentences.idiomatic: Huangchu 3 assigned a king's younger sons by secondary consorts the rank of village duke, an heir-apparent's younger brothers by secondary consorts the rank of precinct marquis, and a duke's or marquis's younger sons by secondary consorts the rank of precinct baron.

sentences.chinese: 劉備章武元年，亦以郡國封建諸王，或遙採嘉名，不由檢土地所出。
sentences.literal: In Liu Bei's Zhangwu first year, he likewise used commanderies and kingdoms to enfeoff the various kings; some took fine titles from afar, without examining what the lands produced.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhangwu 1 watched Liu Bei enfeoff his kinsmen with commandery-sized kingdoms, sometimes borrowing glamorous Central Plain toponyms that bore little relation to local revenue.

sentences.chinese: 其戶二十萬，男女口九十萬。
sentences.literal: Its households were two hundred thousand; male and female mouths nine hundred thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: That realm counted two hundred thousand households and nine hundred thousand persons all told.

sentences.chinese: 孫權赤烏五年，亦取中州嘉號封建諸王。
sentences.literal: In Sun Quan's Chiwu fifth year, he likewise took fine designations from the Central Plain to enfeoff the various kings.
sentences.idiomatic: In his fifth Chiwu year Sun Quan did the same, granting his kinsmen splendid Central-Plain sobriquets.

sentences.chinese: 其戶五十二萬三千，男女口二百四十萬。
sentences.literal: Its households were five hundred twenty-three thousand; male and female mouths two million four hundred thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: His domains mustered 523,000 households and 2,400,000 people.

sentences.chinese: 晉文帝爲晉王，命裴秀等建立五等之制，惟安平郡公孚邑萬戶，制度如魏諸王。
sentences.literal: When Jin Wendi was King of Jin, he ordered Pei Xiu and others to erect the five-grade system; only the Commandery Duke of Anping, Fu, had a fief of ten thousand households; his institutions matched Wei's kings.
sentences.idiomatic: As Jin's king-maker Sima Zhao ordered Pei Xiu to draft the five noble ranks: only Sima Fu, duke of Anping commandery, kept the full ten-thousand-household scale befitting a Wei royal.

sentences.chinese: 其餘縣公邑千八百戶，地方七十五里；
sentences.literal: The rest of the district dukes (xianguo gong) had fiefs of one thousand eight hundred households; the territory seventy-five li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Other county-level dukes held 1,800 households across seventy-five li to the side.

sentences.chinese: 大國侯邑千六百戶，地方七十里；
sentences.literal: A great-state marquis had a fief of one thousand six hundred households; the territory seventy li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Senior-grade marquises drew 1,600 households over seventy li.

sentences.chinese: 次國侯邑千四百戶，地方六十五里；
sentences.literal: A secondary-state marquis had a fief of one thousand four hundred households; the territory sixty-five li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Next-rank marquises held 1,400 households across sixty-five li.

sentences.chinese: 大國伯邑千二百戶，地方六十里；
sentences.literal: A great-state earl (bo) had a fief of one thousand two hundred households; the territory sixty li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Senior earls received 1,200 households within sixty li.

sentences.chinese: 次國伯邑千戶，地方五十五里；
sentences.literal: A secondary-state earl had a fief of one thousand households; the territory fifty-five li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Junior earls kept a thousand households spread over fifty-five li.

sentences.chinese: 大國子邑八百戶，地方五十里；
sentences.literal: A great-state viscount (zi) had a fief of eight hundred households; the territory fifty li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Senior viscounts had eight hundred households inside fifty li.

sentences.chinese: 次國子邑六百戶，地方四十五里；
sentences.literal: A secondary-state viscount had a fief of six hundred households; the territory forty-five li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Lesser viscounts owned six hundred households across forty-five li.

sentences.chinese: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。
sentences.literal: A baron (nan) had a fief of four hundred households; the territory forty li square on each side.
sentences.idiomatic: Lowest baronies stopped at four hundred households and forty li.

sentences.chinese: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。
sentences.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taishi first year, he enfeoffed the various kings with commanderies as their kingdoms.
sentences.idiomatic: Taishi 1 made each prince's kingdom co-extensive with an entire commandery.

sentences.chinese: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；
sentences.literal: Twenty thousand households in the fief is a great state; it establishes upper, middle, and lower armies—five thousand soldiers.
sentences.idiomatic: A great kingdom—20,000 registered households—fielded upper, middle, and lower brigades totaling 5,000 men.

sentences.chinese: 邑萬戶爲次國，置上軍下軍，兵三千人；
sentences.literal: Ten thousand households in the fief is a secondary state; it establishes upper and lower armies—three thousand soldiers.
sentences.idiomatic: Secondary realms of ten thousand households maintained upper and lower corps with 3,000 troops.

sentences.chinese: 五千戶爲小國，置一軍，兵千五百人。
sentences.literal: Five thousand households is a small state; it establishes one army—one thousand five hundred soldiers.
sentences.idiomatic: Petty kingdoms of 5,000 families mustered a single army of 1,500.

sentences.chinese: 王不之國，官於京師。
sentences.literal: The kings did not go to their kingdoms; they held office in the capital.
sentences.idiomatic: Princes stayed in Luoyang on court salary rather than residing in their nominal realms.

sentences.chinese: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。
sentences.literal: The five-grade system was abolished; dukes and marquises with fiefs of ten thousand households or more were great states, five thousand or more secondary states, fewer than five thousand small states.
sentences.idiomatic: After the five-rank scheme lapsed, ducal or marquisal estates of ten thousand households or more counted as great polities, those from five thousand upward as secondary, and those below five thousand as small.

sentences.chinese: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。
sentences.literal: In Taikang first year, when Wu was pacified, in the main there were two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty households; sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three persons.
sentences.idiomatic: Taikang 1, the year Wu fell, the empire tallied roughly 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths.

sentences.chinese: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。
sentences.literal: But the various kingdoms east of the Yangtze all took one-third [of their commanderies' revenue]; after Yuan Emperor crossed the Yangtze, in Taixing first year, they first instituted taking one-ninth.
sentences.idiomatic: South of the river every apanage skimmed a third of its host commandery until Yuan crossed; Taixing 1 trimmed the royal share to one-ninth.

sentences.chinese: 案禹貢豫州之地。
sentences.literal: This follows the land of Yu's Tribute's Yu Province.
sentences.idiomatic: The chapter tracks the Yu Province demarcated in the "Tribute of Yu."

sentences.chinese: 及漢武帝，初置司隸校尉，所部三輔、三河諸郡。
sentences.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, he first established the Colonel Director of Retainers; what it commanded were the three adjuncts, Three Rivers, and the various commanderies.
sentences.idiomatic: Han Wudi created the Colonel Director of Retainers to oversee the three metropolitan adjuncts and the Three Rivers commanderies.

sentences.chinese: 其界西得雍州之京兆、馮翊、扶風三郡，北得冀州之河東、河內二郡，東得豫州之弘農、河南二郡，郡凡七。
sentences.literal: Its bounds: west it took three commanderies from Yongzhou—Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng; north it took two from Jizhou—Hedong, Henei; east it took two from Yuzhou—Hongnong, Henan—in all seven commanderies.
sentences.idiomatic: The colonel's seven commanderies drew Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng from Yongzhou, Hedong and Henei from Jizhou, and Hongnong and Henan from Yuzhou.

sentences.chinese: 位望隆于牧伯，[6]銀印青綬。
sentences.literal: Dignity and repute surpassed those of shepherds and chiefs; silver seal and green ribbon.
sentences.idiomatic: The colonel outranked provincial shepherds, badge by silver seal and green ribbon.

sentences.chinese: 及光武都洛陽，司隸所部與前漢不異。
sentences.literal: When Guangwu made his capital at Luoyang, what the Colonel Director of Retainers commanded did not differ from Western Han.
sentences.idiomatic: Guangwu's move to Luoyang left the colonel's remit matching Western Han's footprint.

sentences.chinese: 魏氏受禪，即都漢宮，司隸所部河南、河東、河內、弘農并冀州之平陽，合五郡，置司州。
sentences.literal: When Wei received the abdication, it immediately took the Han palace as capital; what the Colonel commanded—Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, together with Pingyang from Jizhou—five commanderies combined—was set up as Sizhou.
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Wei inherited Luoyang's palaces, folded Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, and Pingyang commandery from Jizhou into a five-commandery Sizhou.

sentences.chinese: 晉仍居魏都，乃以三輔還屬雍州，分河南立滎陽，分雍州之京兆立上洛，廢東郡立頓丘，遂定名司州，以司隸校尉統之。
sentences.literal: Jin still dwelled in Wei's capital; therefore it returned the three adjuncts to Yongzhou, split Henan to establish Xingyang, split Jingzhao from Yongzhou to establish Shangluo, abolished Dong commandery and established Dunqiu—thereupon the name Sizhou was fixed, governed by the Colonel Director of Retainers.
sentences.idiomatic: Western Jin stayed put but reassigned the three Qin adjuncts back to Yong, carved Xingyang out of Henan, Shangluo out of Jingzhao, traded Dong commandery for Dunqiu, and locked the new layout under the colonel's eye.

sentences.chinese: 州統郡一十二，縣一百，戶四十七萬五千七百。
sentences.literal: The zhou governed twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, and four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred households.
sentences.idiomatic: This Sizhou ruled twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, and 475,700 households.

sentences.literal: The transmitted text marks a seventh scholium.
sentences.idiomatic: Here the edition inserts a marginal gloss in the commentary tradition.

sentences.chinese: 河南郡
sentences.literal: Henan commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Henan commandery.

sentences.chinese: 〈漢置。
sentences.literal: The Han court created this commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: The Han founding administration chartered Henan commandery here.

sentences.chinese: 統縣十二，戶一十一萬四千四百。
sentences.literal: It governed twelve counties and had one hundred fourteen thousand four hundred households.
sentences.idiomatic: It oversaw twelve counties and 114,400 registered households.

sentences.chinese: 置尹。〉
sentences.literal: A metropolitan prefect (yin) headed the commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: The senior magistrate bore the metropolitan yin title.

sentences.chinese: 洛陽
sentences.literal: Luoyang.
sentences.idiomatic: Luoyang.

sentences.chinese: 〈置尉。
sentences.literal: The county seat stationed a captain (wei).
sentences.idiomatic: A county captain kept order in the county seat.

sentences.chinese: 五部、三市。
sentences.literal: Five wards, three markets.
sentences.idiomatic: Five inner wards and three market wards.

sentences.chinese: 東西七里，南北九里。
sentences.literal: Seven li east-west, nine li north-south.
sentences.idiomatic: The walled core stretched seven li east–west and nine north–south.

sentences.chinese: 東有建春、東陽、清明三門，南有開陽、平昌、宣陽、建陽四門，西有廣陽、西明、閶闔三門，北有大夏、廣莫二門。
sentences.literal: East had three gates—Jianchun, Dongyang, Qingming; south had four—Kaiyang, Pingchang, Xuanyang, Jianyang; west had three gates—Guangyang, Ximing, Changhe; north had two gates—Daxia, Guangmo.
sentences.idiomatic: The east wall opened Jianchun, Dongyang, and Qingming; the south wall Kaiyang, Pingchang, Xuanyang, and Jianyang; the west Guangyang, Ximing, and Changhe; the north only Daxia and Guangmo.

sentences.chinese: 司隸校尉、河南尹及百官列城內也。〉
sentences.literal: The Colonel Director of Retainers, the Henan yin, and the full bureaucracy were quartered inside the walls.
sentences.idiomatic: Colonel, prefect, and the organs of government all fit within that enceinte.

sentences.chinese: 河南
sentences.literal: Henan [county].
sentences.idiomatic: Henan county.

sentences.chinese: 〈周東都王城郟鄏也。〉
sentences.literal: It was the Zhou eastern-capital royal city at Jia-Ru (Wangcheng).
sentences.idiomatic: This ground had been the Zhou eastern capital Wangcheng in the Jia-Ru quarter.

sentences.chinese: 鞏
sentences.literal: Gong.
sentences.idiomatic: Gong county.

sentences.chinese: 〈周孝王封周桓公孫惠公於鞏，號東周，故戰國時有東、西周號。
sentences.literal: King Xiao of Zhou enfeoffed Duke Hui, grandson of Duke Huan of Zhou, at Gong with the epithet Eastern Zhou, so the Warring States era knew both Eastern and Western Zhou polities.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhou King Xiao made the Gong line a cadet house nicknamed Eastern Zhou, which is why Warring States maps speak of eastern and western Zhou polities.

sentences.chinese: 芒山、首陽其界也。〉
sentences.literal: Mount Mang and Mount Shouyang marked its marches.
sentences.idiomatic: Its border ran along Mount Mang and Mount Shouyang.

sentences.chinese: 河陰 新安
sentences.literal: Heyin, Xin'an.
sentences.idiomatic: Heyin and Xin'an.

sentences.chinese: 〈函谷關所居。〉
sentences.literal: Hangu Pass stood on this ground.
sentences.idiomatic: This was the terrain on which Hangu Pass sat.

sentences.chinese: 成皋
sentences.literal: Chenggao.
sentences.idiomatic: Chenggao.

sentences.chinese: 〈有關，鄭之武牢。〉
sentences.literal: It held a barrier: Wulao of Zheng.
sentences.idiomatic: This county lodged Zheng's old Wulao fortress.

sentences.chinese: 緱氏
sentences.literal: Goushi.
sentences.idiomatic: Goushi.

sentences.chinese: 〈有劉聚，周大夫劉子邑。
sentences.literal: It contained the Liu cluster—the seat of Zhou grandee Liu Zi.
sentences.idiomatic: The Liu quarter preserved the estate of Zhou's ministerial Liu lineage.

sentences.chinese: 有延壽城、仙人祠。〉
sentences.literal: It had Yanshou city and an Immortal's shrine.
sentences.idiomatic: Yanshou town and an Immortal shrine stood here.

sentences.chinese: 陽城
sentences.literal: Yangcheng.
sentences.idiomatic: Yangcheng.

sentences.chinese: 〈有鄂阪關。
sentences.literal: It maintained the Eban pass.
sentences.idiomatic: Traffic here was choked through the Eban defile.

sentences.chinese: 此邑是爲地中，夏至景尺五寸。
sentences.literal: This settlement is taken as earth's center; at summer solstice the gnomon shadow is one chi five cun.
sentences.idiomatic: Surveyors deemed this town the midpoint of the world—summer solstice noon shadow one chi and five cun.

sentences.chinese: 有陽城山、箕山，許由墓在焉。〉
sentences.literal: It counted Mount Yangcheng and Mount Ji, and Xu You's tomb lay among them.
sentences.idiomatic: Mount Yangcheng, Mount Ji, and Xu You's grave all fell within this county.

sentences.chinese: 新城
sentences.literal: Xincheng.
sentences.idiomatic: Xincheng.

sentences.chinese: 〈有延壽關。
sentences.literal: It set a barrier at Yanshou.
sentences.idiomatic: A Yanshou gate controlled access along the route.

sentences.chinese: 故戎蠻子之國。〉
sentences.literal: It was formerly the polity of the Rong Manzi lordling.
sentences.idiomatic: This ground had once been the tiny realm of the Rong Manzi.

sentences.chinese: 陸渾
sentences.literal: Luhun.
sentences.idiomatic: Luhun.

sentences.chinese: 〈故蠻子國，楚莊王伐陸渾是也。〉
sentences.literal: It was the old Manzi state—the very Luhun whom King Zhuang of Chu campaigned against.
sentences.idiomatic: Here stood the Manzi chiefdom later overrun in King Zhuang of Chu's expedition against Luhun.

sentences.chinese: 梁
sentences.literal: Liang.
sentences.idiomatic: Liang county town.

sentences.chinese: 〈戰國時謂爲南梁，別少梁也。〉
sentences.literal: The Warring States age knew it as Southern Liang, not to be confused with Shaoliang.
sentences.idiomatic: Warring States geographers distinguished this Southern Liang from Shaoliang upriver.

sentences.chinese: 陽翟
sentences.literal: Yangzhai.
sentences.idiomatic: Yangzhai.

sentences.chinese: 滎陽郡
sentences.literal: Xingyang commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Xingyang commandery.

sentences.chinese: 〈泰始二年置。
sentences.literal: Jin created this commandery in the second year of Taishi.
sentences.idiomatic: Western Jin partitioned the map anew in Taishi 2 to seat Xingyang commandery.
